a_records.quote: Theorem 1. Let X1 , . . . , Xn (X1∗ , . . . , Xn∗ ) be independent and non-negative random variables with Xi ∼ r(x; αi , βi ) (Xi∗ ∼ r(x; αi∗ , βi )), i = 1, . . . , n. Further, suppose that Ip1 , . . . , Ipn (Ip∗1 , . . . , Ip∗n ) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xi 's (Xi∗ 's), with E[Ipi ] = pi (E[Ip∗i ] = p∗i ), i = 1, . . . , n. Assume that the following conditions hold: (i) r(x; α, β) is increasing [decreasing] and convex in α for any β and any x > 0; (ii) ∂r(x;α,β)/∂α is decreasing (increasing) in β for any α and any x > 0. Then, for (α, β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+ ) and (α∗ , β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+ ), we have Πi=1..n p∗i ≤ Πi=1..n pi and (α1 , . . . , αn ) ⪯w [⪯w ](α1∗ , . . . , αn∗ ) =⇒ Y1:n∗ ≤hr Y1:n .
a_records.family: General two-parameter severity model: Xi has hazard rate r(x; αi, βi); claim amounts Yi = Ipi Xi with Ipi ~ Bernoulli(pi); Y1:n = smallest claim amount (minimum of the portfolio)
a_records.compared: parameter vectors α vs α* (β common); occurrence probabilities p vs p*

b_records.quote: Theorem 1. Let X1, . . . , Xn (X1*, . . . , Xn*) be independent and non-negative random variables with Xi ∼ r(x; αi, βi) (Xi* ∼ r(x; αi*, βi)), i = 1, . . . , n. Further, suppose that Ip1, . . . , Ipn (Ip*1, . . . , Ip*n) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xi's (Xi*'s), with E[Ipi] = pi (E[Ip*i] = p*i), i = 1, . . . , n. Assume that the following conditions hold: (i) r(x; α, β) is increasing [decreasing] and convex in α for any β and any x > 0; (ii) ∂r(x;α,β)/∂α is decreasing (increasing) in β for any α and any x > 0. Then, for (α, β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+) and (α*, β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+), we have Π_{i=1}^n p*i ≤ Π_{i=1}^n pi and (α1, . . . , αn) ≼w [≼^w] (α1*, . . . , αn*) ⇒ Y1:n* ≤hr Y1:n.
